value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Santa Cruz/Santa Cruz County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: SolarAPP+ Approval Document (generated only when approved)
SolarAPP+ Inspection Checklist (generated only when approved; must be signed by a field solar representative confirming completion prior to inspection)
City of Santa Cruz permit number (emailed after Solar APP+ sends the Approval Document and Inspection Checklist to the City)

value: Have a field solar representative verify and sign the Inspection Checklist confirming completion prior to inspection
Call (831) 420-5110 to schedule an inspection for an issued permit; inspections are posted by 8am the morning of the scheduled date
Requests made after 2pm do not qualify for next-business-day scheduling and are instead scheduled for the second business day
The Permit, SolarAPP+ Approval Document, and Inspection Checklist must be printed and kept at the job site at all times for inspection
A reinspection fee applies if work is not ready, documents aren't on site, or revisions weren't completed via SolarAPP+ before scheduling

value.notes: The City's own page is titled 'Instant and Affordable Solar Permit Available through SolarAPP+' and states 'For the City of Santa Cruz, SolarApp+ will instantly issue the permit after payment is complete.'

other_conditions: Only new rooftop solar PV on detached one- and two-family dwellings, townhomes, and related accessory structures (e.g. garage or ADU)
Only licensed contractors may use SolarAPP+; non-licensed owner-builders must apply for a regular Solar Permit through the standard plan check process
No stated total wattage limit, but service panel equipment is capped at up to 400A main service, 225A service disconnect switches, and 225A busbars
Properties with active code compliance cases, unverified compliance complaints, voided permits, or location in a flood zone may not participate

permit_fees.notes: The City's own page states 'all applicable permit fees will be assessed per the City of Santa Cruz Master Fee Schedule' but gives no specific dollar figure directly on this page.
